title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover under high load-shedding
author: Elena Park
description: Context: an on-call incident on 2026-02-18 (SUP-4532) showed the SLO enforcer could thrash between regional circuit-breaker and load-shedding states during a burst of cross-region traffic, causing cascade failovers and increased latency for dedicated customers. This hotfix reduces thrashing and stabilizes ordering during aggressive load-shedding so regional failover only occurs when downstream capacity is truly exhausted. Changeset overview: adjust enforcer backoff/hysteresis, add tie-break ordering to failover decisions, reduce cache invalidations during circuit transitions, and add extra guards against concurrent state transitions. Test plan: unit tests for ordering and hysteresis, integration test simulating region A->B failover under load-shedding, canary rollout to 3% of traffic, smoke tests for dedicated and hosted flows. Deployment notes: deploy to staging, run chaos scenario for 30m, then progressive rollout to regions with canary followed by 50%/100%. Rollback plan: revert the migration commit and scale down canary if fail rates regress. Checklist: [x] reproduce incident locally, [x] add unit/integration tests, [x] run canary in staging, [x] monitor SLO/regression dashboards, [x] coordinate on-call. Related work: builds on ENG-3109 (slo-enforcer metrics) and ENG-3298 (priority queue adjustments).
